title: How to Navigate Grandma’s Thanksgiving Dinner Without Spiking Your Post-Meal Glucose—Especially If You’re Newly Diagnosed With Prediabetes at 58
description: A step-by-step, plate-by-plate guide to making real-time food swaps, timing insulin or meds, and using fiber-first sequencing to blunt glucose spikes during multigenerational holiday meals.
primaryKeyword: manage post-meal glucose at family dinners

title: 7 Hidden Sodium Traps in ‘Healthy’ Holiday Side Dishes That Raise Systolic BP in Adults 62–76 With Stage 1 Hypertension
description: Exposes unsuspected high-sodium culprits—like herb-infused roasted carrots, ‘low-fat’ stuffing, and fermented cabbage salads—and offers low-sodium, flavor-forward alternatives backed by 24-hour urinary sodium studies.
primaryKeyword: hidden sodium in holiday side dishes

title: Can You Enjoy Holiday Pie Without Triggering Acid Reflux at Night? A 3-Step Timing & Texture Strategy for Adults 65+ With GERD
description: Explores the science of gastric emptying delays in aging, identifies pie ingredients most likely to cause nocturnal reflux, and outlines a precise pre- and post-pie protocol—including upright posture timing and texture-modified serving suggestions.
primaryKeyword: prevent nighttime acid reflux after pie

title: 12 Science-Backed Ways to Reduce Post-Holiday Inflammation in Just 5 Days—Targeting CRP, IL-6, and Endothelial Function in Adults 55–72
description: A clinically grounded, action-oriented protocol—including specific polyphenol-rich foods, cold-water immersion timing, walking cadence targets, and breathwork intervals—validated in a pilot RCT measuring inflammatory biomarkers pre- and post-holiday season.
